- Overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast periods; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent history shows sustained upward trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price increases; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak observed in prior 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecasted values before final adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: forecast often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust forward by 1–2 days if true price is rising steadily.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5 days are above 75% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
